title: SQL Views and Built-in Functions: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on views and materialized views, then the everyday scalar functions: string, date/time, CASE/COALESCE/NULLIF, CAST and rounding. Covers mental models, usage, common mistakes and a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Views and Materialized Views
points: A view is a saved SELECT with a name; it stores no data and re-runs its query on every access
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v AS SELECT ...; DROP VIEW v; the replacement must keep existing column names and order (PostgreSQL)

Materialized view stores the result physically: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv AS SELECT ...; it goes stale until REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv (CONCURRENTLY needs a unique index and avoids blocking reads)
View vs materialized view: always fresh and slower vs fast reads but stale; only a materialized view can be indexed
Gotcha: SELECT * in a view is expanded at creation, so columns added later to the base table do not appear; simple views are updatable, but those with GROUP BY, DISTINCT or joins usually are not

chapters.title: String Functions
points: CONCAT(a,b) treats NULL as empty; the || operator returns NULL if any operand is NULL
UPPER, LOWER, LENGTH and TRIM (plus LTRIM/RTRIM) clean and measure text; LENGTH counts characters in PostgreSQL but bytes in some engines
SUBSTRING(s, start, len) is 1-indexed, not 0-indexed; LEFT(s,n) and RIGHT(s,n) take from the ends
REPLACE(s, from, to) replaces all occurrences; POSITION('x' IN s) or INSTR returns 0 when not found
LIKE '%abc' with a leading wildcard or LOWER(col) in WHERE cannot use a plain index; use a functional index or ILIKE carefully

chapters.title: Date and Time Functions
points: CURRENT_DATE returns a date, NOW() / CURRENT_TIMESTAMP return a timestamp with time zone; they are fixed for the whole transaction
EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ts) pulls a part; DATE_TRUNC('month', ts) rounds down to the start of the period (used for monthly GROUP BY)
Date arithmetic: ts + INTERVAL '7 days'; date - date gives an integer day count; timestamp - timestamp gives an interval
AGE(a,b) gives years/months/days; MySQL uses DATEDIFF(a,b) and DATE_ADD(d, INTERVAL 1 DAY) instead
Gotcha: BETWEEN on a timestamp column with an end date misses that day after midnight; use ts >= '2026-01-01' AND ts < '2026-02-01'

chapters.title: CASE, COALESCE and NULLIF
points: Searched CASE: CASE WHEN cond THEN x WHEN cond2 THEN y ELSE z END; first true branch wins, and a missing ELSE returns NULL
Simple CASE: CASE col WHEN 'a' THEN 1 END compares with = only, so it can never match NULL
COALESCE(a, b, c) returns the first non-NULL argument; use it for defaults, e.g. COALESCE(discount, 0)
NULLIF(a, b) returns NULL when a = b, else a; the classic use is x / NULLIF(y, 0) to avoid divide-by-zero
Gotcha: all CASE branches must return compatible types, and NULL + 1 is NULL, so wrap nullable columns in COALESCE before arithmetic

chapters.title: CAST and Numeric Rounding
points: CAST(x AS INTEGER) is standard SQL; PostgreSQL also accepts x::integer; a bad value such as CAST('abc' AS INT) raises an error
Casting a decimal to INTEGER rounds in PostgreSQL but truncates in MySQL and SQL Server; check your engine
ROUND(x, 2) rounds to 2 decimals; a negative scale works too, ROUND(1234, -2) = 1200; CEIL goes up, FLOOR goes down, TRUNC cuts toward zero
Integer division truncates: 7/2 = 3; write 7/2.0 or CAST(7 AS NUMERIC)/2 to get 3.5
Use NUMERIC/DECIMAL for money, never FLOAT, because float rounding errors accumulate; ROUND(x,2) on a float may also fail in PostgreSQL

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Views and Functions
points: Views: CREATE [OR REPLACE] VIEW, CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW, REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW [CONCURRENTLY], DROP VIEW
Strings: CONCAT vs || NULL behaviour, SUBSTRING 1-indexed, TRIM, REPLACE, LIKE leading wildcard skips index
Dates: NOW(), CURRENT_DATE, EXTRACT, DATE_TRUNC, INTERVAL arithmetic, half-open range filter
Null handling: CASE (else NULL), COALESCE for defaults, NULLIF(y,0) for safe division
Casting and rounding: CAST/::, ROUND(x,n), CEIL/FLOOR/TRUNC, 7/2=3 vs 7/2.0=3.5, NUMERIC for money
